experience-list.short-description: Jurni is a web application that helps users clarify their career goals through a comprehensive profile assessment (personality, motivations, needs, skills), then identify careers that truly align with that profile. The goal is to turn a often vague reflection (“What career suits me?”) into concrete, personalized, and actionable recommendations.

content-1.title: Problems I solve with this project

content-list.list-item-1: Make career guidance more reliable and less based on gut feeling.
content-list.list-item-2: Combine multiple dimensions (psychology, motivations, skills, constraints) in a single experience.
content-list.list-item-3: Reduce the time between “I'm questioning my path” and “I have realistic options.”
content-list.list-item-4: Offer a smooth, understandable, and bilingual experience, even for a non-technical audience.

content-2.title: Technical stack used for this project

content-list.list-item-1:
Frontend: Next.js (React) + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS
For a fast, modern, and maintainable interface.
content-list.list-item-2:
Backend API: FastAPI (Python)
To expose robust, well-structured, and documented endpoints.
content-list.list-item-3:
Database: MongoDB
Suited to evolving user data and assessment results.
content-list.list-item-4:
Cache: Redis
To speed up responses and reduce load on the main database.
content-list.list-item-5:
AI / orchestration: LangGraph + LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic)
To manage multi-step conversational flows and personalized analyses.
content-list.list-item-6:
API documentation: Swagger/OpenAPI
To facilitate testing, integration, and product/tech collaboration.
content-list.list-item-7:
Payments: Stripe
Secure handling of credit purchases.
content-list.list-item-8:
Infra / deployment: Docker + Docker Compose + Traefik
For consistent (dev/prod), scalable environments that are easier to operate.
content-list.list-item-9:
Observability & product: Mixpanel + Langfuse
To track usage, AI flow quality, and improve continuously.
content-list.list-item-10: Additional services: Resend (emails), Google APIs (integrations), etc.

content-3.title: Technical choices and why they are relevant
content-3.content: I chose this architecture to balance delivery speed, product quality, and scalability:

content-list.list-item-1: Next.js + TypeScript secure the frontend and accelerate the development of complex interfaces.
content-list.list-item-2: FastAPI provides a performant, clear API that is naturally compatible with OpenAPI documentation.
content-list.list-item-3: MongoDB is well suited to a product handling rich and evolving data structures.
content-list.list-item-4: Redis improves perceived responsiveness for users.
content-list.list-item-5: LangGraph properly structures AI workflows (conversation, extraction, scoring), making behavior more reliable than a simple single prompt.
content-list.list-item-6: Docker standardizes execution across all environments and reduces gaps between local and production.
content-list.list-item-7: Mixpanel and Langfuse provide robust observability tools suited to the scale of a SaaS product.

content-list.list-item-1: A more personalized and useful user experience for career decision-making.
content-list.list-item-2: More consistent career recommendations thanks to cross-referencing multiple signals.
content-list.list-item-3: Better product conversion through a clear journey, a credit model, and high-value analyses.
content-list.list-item-4: A solid technical foundation to iterate quickly, add new assessments, and evolve the product.

experience-list.long-title: Simulforge / Simulphone — Training suite for call centers
experience-list.short-description:
I contributed to the SimulSuite, an ecosystem made up of two complementary web applications and a shared library, sold under B2B licenses to training centers and client organizations.
My role: bug fixes, development of new features (frontend and backend), and ongoing maintenance of both applications and the common library.
Note: the applications are licensed and access-restricted; I cannot include screenshots.

content-list.list-item-1:
SimulPhone:
Audience: Trainees and trainers (call centers)
Role: Call simulator to practice handling stress and difficult situations on the phone
content-list.list-item-2:
SimulForge:
Audience: Internal teams (back office)
Role: Client administration, training sessions, and creation of educational content used in SimulPhone
content-list.list-item-3:
SimulLibrary:
Audience: Developers
Role: Shared code (services, models, components) to avoid duplication between the two applications (SimulPhone and SimulForge)

content-list.list-item-1: For call centers: train agents in a safe environment, with no impact on real customers, using realistic scenarios (stressful calls, emotional states, ambient sounds).
content-list.list-item-2: For trainers: run live sessions, monitor trainees, listen to/replay recordings, and analyze performance.
content-list.list-item-3: For the publisher: manage a licensed client base, configure training programs, and maintain a catalog of simulations (scenes, scripts, personas, puzzles, etc.) from a centralized back office.

content-3.title: Technical stack used for this project

content-list.list-item-5: PeerJS — peer-to-peer audio communication for call simulations
content-list.list-item-6: Socket.io — real-time (trainer audio room, connected trainee tracking)
content-list.list-item-9: MediaRecorder API — recording of simulated calls
content-list.list-item-11: Sequelize — ORM on MariaDB (business data: clients, users, sessions, scenes, licenses, permissions…)
content-list.list-item-13: Socket.io — real-time orchestration of simulations (trainer/trainee connections, call status)
content-list.list-item-14: JWT + bcrypt — authentication and access security
content-list.list-item-17: Shared HTTP services (users, sessions, scenes, callers, permissions, translations…)
content-list.list-item-19: Reusable UI components, interceptors (JWT token, language)
content-list.list-item-21: Docker — images per application and per environment (prod, staging, demo, local)
content-list.list-item-22: GitLab CI/CD — lint, security analysis (SAST), frontend build, Docker image generation

content-4.title: Key features of the training suite

content-list.list-item-1: Call simulation with real-time audio flow, ringtones, ambient sounds, and recording
content-list.list-item-4: Complementary workshops (escape game, puzzles, educational modules)
content-list.list-item-5: Client and organization management (users, granular permissions)
content-list.list-item-7: Creation and editing of simulations (scenes, phases, personas, scripts, emotional states, soundtracks)
content-list.list-item-8: Pedagogy, resources, localization, statistics, and administration modules

content-list.list-item-1: Angular monorepo (2 apps + lib): A single frontend repository, coordinated builds, shared code via the library
content-list.list-item-2: Simulsuite Library: Avoids duplicating services and models; a fix benefits both apps
content-list.list-item-3: MariaDB + Sequelize: Structured relational data (clients, sessions, permissions) with migrations and typed queries
content-list.list-item-4: MongoDB as a complement: Flexibility for certain document-based content
content-list.list-item-5: Socket.io + PeerJS: Real-time for trainer control; direct audio between trainee and simulated scenario
content-list.list-item-6: Granular permissions: Each role (trainer, admin, editor…) only accesses authorized features
content-list.list-item-7: Docker + GitLab CI: Reproducible deployments and automated pipelines per environment

experience-list.long-title: Marches-publics.com — access to 100% of public tenders
experience-list.short-description: Marches-publics.com is a platform that centralizes all public tenders published in France, including those not listed on official channels, and allows companies to configure targeted alerts, instantly access technical documentation (DCE), and track award history. My mission on this project: completely redesign the user interface to modernize it, make it more readable, and improve the overall experience for professional users. The redesign is currently in progress and has not yet been deployed to production.

content-list.list-item-1: Give an aging interface a modern, smooth, and consistent experience that meets current web standards.
content-list.list-item-2: Improve readability and visual hierarchy so non-technical users (sales reps, consultants, architects…) can navigate without friction.
content-list.list-item-3: Clean up a codebase that had become bloated over time: remove redundancies, delete unused code, reduce the overall weight of the application.
content-list.list-item-4: Establish a solid, structured, and maintainable frontend foundation to help the product team iterate more easily in the future.
content-list.list-item-5: Make the interface suitable for all screens, especially for users on the go.

content-2.title: Technical stack used for this project

content-list.list-item-1: Frontend: Angular + TypeScript — For a robust, modular architecture suited to complex business applications maintained over the long term.
content-list.list-item-2: Mockup: Lovable, a no-code/AI design tool used to establish the visual foundations of the new interface before integration.

content-list.list-item-1: Starting from a mockup created on Lovable made it possible to quickly validate the visual direction and interface choices before writing code — a concrete time saver and a way to limit back-and-forth between design and development.
content-list.list-item-2:
For integration, Angular was the natural choice: it is an opinionated framework that enforces a clear structure and strict conventions. This is a real advantage in a redesign context, as it ensures readable and consistent code, even when multiple developers work on the project. Combined with TypeScript, a language that catches errors before runtime, it delivers a reliable interface that is easy to evolve without accumulating technical debt.
This choice is also consistent with the existing stack: reusing the same technology as the previous version made it possible to migrate progressively, without starting from scratch or destabilizing what already works.

content-list.list-item-1: A modernized, clearer, and more pleasant interface that better reflects the quality of the service offered.
content-list.list-item-2: A lighter and more performant application thanks to a deep cleanup of the existing code (removal of redundancies, dead code removal).
content-list.list-item-3: A redesigned user experience to reduce friction and speed up key journeys (search, access to DCE, alert management).
content-list.list-item-4: A cleaned-up and maintainable codebase that will facilitate future product evolution.
content-list.list-item-5: Better adaptability across devices for professionals often on the move.

experience-list.long-title: Showcase website — Atelier Jean-Claude Larrivé (upholsterer & interior decorator)
experience-list.short-description: Professional website for Jean-Claude Larrivé, an artisan upholsterer and interior decorator in Auxerre (Yonne). The site showcases his expertise, portfolio, and services (chair restoration, interior decoration, introductory workshops), with a clear goal: be visible locally and make it easy to get in touch (quotes, advice).

content-list.list-item-1: Local visibility: an artisan without a web presence loses inquiries from clients searching for an upholsterer in Auxerre or nearby (Avallon, markets, etc.).
content-list.list-item-2: Credibility: highlight over 35 years of experience, the workshop, and concrete work (armchairs, sofas, curtains, blinds).
content-list.list-item-3: Conversion: make it easy to get in touch (form, phone, email, location).
content-list.list-item-4: Education: inform visitors about upholstery workshops offered at the atelier.

content-2.title: Technical stack used for this project

content-list.list-item-2: Tailwind CSS 4 + DaisyUI (custom theme in the atelier's colors)
content-list.list-item-3: Google Fonts (Parisienne, Zeyada) for an artisan visual identity
content-list.list-item-4: EmailJS: contact form without a dedicated backend (client-side email sending)
content-list.list-item-5: Leaflet + react-leaflet + OpenStreetMap: interactive map of the workshop (dynamic loading, no SSR)
content-list.list-item-6: YouTube API: embedded video on the Portfolio page (blinds, installation)
content-list.list-item-8: Dedicated SEO component per page (title, description, keywords, canonical)
content-list.list-item-9: Schema.org structured data (LocalBusiness, Person, Organization) for local SEO
content-list.list-item-10: next-sitemap — automatic sitemap and robots.txt generation at build time
content-list.list-item-11: Legal notices and terms of use pages
content-list.list-item-13: Vercel hosting (suited to Next.js, simple deployment)
content-list.list-item-14: Static site / minimal server logic: low hosting cost and light maintenance

content-list.list-item-1: Home: Introduction, workshop map, contact call-to-action
content-list.list-item-2: Portfolio: Photo galleries (seating, other creations), responsive layout, trade video
content-list.list-item-3: Materials: Fabrics, traditional craftsmanship, eco-friendly pictograms (Green Line, rPET, etc.)
content-list.list-item-4: Workshops: Training offer at the atelier (pricing, terms)
content-list.list-item-5: Contact: Form, contact details, Google Maps link
content-list.list-item-6: Responsive navigation (mobile burger menu), polished layout (polaroid-style galleries positioned differently depending on screen size).

content-list.list-item-1: Next.js: Fast pages, native SEO, simple routing for a multi-page site
content-list.list-item-2: No custom backend: For a showcase site, EmailJS is enough for contact — less complexity and lower costs
content-list.list-item-3: Enhanced local SEO: Geolocated keywords + JSON-LD to appear on searches like “upholsterer Auxerre”
content-list.list-item-4: Tailwind + DaisyUI: Consistent, responsive UI, customizable without a heavy CSS framework
content-list.list-item-5: Dynamically loaded map: Leaflet does not work with SSR; dynamic import avoids build errors
content-list.list-item-6: Lazy-loaded images: With many galleries, better performance on mobile

content-list.list-item-1: Professional presence for an artisan in a market that is still very local and relationship-driven
content-list.list-item-2: Sales tool: showcase of work and channel for quote requests
content-list.list-item-3: Accessibility: semantic structure, alt text on visuals, form labels
content-list.list-item-4: Scalable foundation: clear architecture to add pages or content without a full redesign

  - EmailJS Privacy Policy: [https://www.emailjs.com/legal/privacy-policy/](https://www.emailjs.com/legal/privacy-policy/). EmailJS acts as a data processor and handles your data in accordance with its own privacy policy.

This data is processed by Google LLC, headquartered in the United States. This transfer is governed by the standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission.
  - Google Privacy Policy: [https://policies.google.com/privacy](https://policies.google.com/privacy)
